_comment: Documented pattern defects that are NOT fixable by editing the regex: hashcat renumbers modes between releases, so the example bundled for a mode can belong to a different algorithm. Each entry is (mode, code) plus why it is tolerated. Anything not listed here is treated as a new regression.

known_issues.reason: hashcat's mode-300 example is the bare 40-hex MySQL323 digest while 'MySQL 4.1+' is the '*FCF7...' star-prefixed form. Both shapes are real; the bundled example describes the sibling format.
The mode-1731 example in patterns.meta.json is truncated (84 chars vs the 94 the regex requires).
The bundled NetNTLMv1 example uses an empty username and 32-hex fields; the pattern models the 48-hex challenge/response form emitted by Responder.
The example for mode 19800 is a $krb5pa$ pre-auth hash, while the pattern covers $krb5asrep$ AES256 replies. Upstream numbering drift.
The generated regex keeps a lookahead requiring '+' or '/' taken literally from the hashcat example; real OpenEdge encodings do not always contain them.
